title: Establish endpoint quality-curve SLI and error-budget burn-rate policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current SLOs are coarse (availability + p95) and do not capture model quality regressions, per-endpoint traffic characteristics, nor support progressive error-budget-driven shedding across regions. This causes teams to either over-provision or face unpredictable throttles during bursts, with insufficient guidance for graceful degradation across model variants and regions.

Goal: Define a measurable, per-endpoint and per-model SLI taxonomy built around a 'quality curve' concept (latency, success, and quality dimensions) and formalize an error-budget burn-rate policy that integrates with multi-region reservation rules, circuit breaker thresholds, and staged load-shedding windows. Deliverables:
- SLI definitions for common endpoint classes (chat, completion, embedding, rerank) including sampling and instrumentation guidance.
- Quality-curve specification: continuous metric banding that relates latency and model-quality (e.g., hallucination/entailment score) to SLO health across ten graded buckets.
- Error-budget burn-rate rules: short-window (1m/5m) and long-window (1h/24h) burn logic; actions for burn-rate > 3x (alert), > 10x (automated mitigation).
- Multi-region reservation + failover policy: per-customer regional reservations, cross-region fallback priority list, and reserved capacity borrow/repay semantics tied to error budget state.
- Circuit breaker matrix: per-route thresholds (latency, error-rate, quality drift) with tiered backoff and automatic rollback to next-compatible model variant or lower-cost profile.
- Load-shedding plan: progressive shed windows (graceful prefix trimming, token-budget throttles, and hard rejections), observability dashboards, and runbook for on-call.
- API and Console contract: new SLO metadata fields and visibility in model/route dashboards for ownership and alerting.

Measurement & Instrumentation:
- SLIs: success_rate, latency_p{50,95,99}, quality_metric (derived from evals per prompt-type), freshness_of_model, and KV_cache_hit_rate. Define sampling rates per route class and a canonical query for SLI ingestion in Prometheus/observability pipeline.
- Buckets: quality-curve maps measured quality_score into SLO weight multipliers to compute a composite health score (route-level).

Acceptance criteria:
1) SLI docs and PromQL queries for each endpoint class checked in to docs and monitoring repo.
2) Error-budget burn-rate rules implemented as alerting policies with simulated replay tests showing correct actions at 3x and 10x thresholds.
3) Console surfaces per-route composite health and remaining error budget.
4) Playbook validated in a canary region: simulated surge triggers progressive shedding and cross-region failover without customer data exposure.

Rollout plan:
Phase 0 (week 1): finalize taxonomy, review with SRE/Platform/Models.
Phase 1 (week 2): instrument SLIs on a small set of non-critical routes; enable dashboards.
Phase 2 (week 3-4): enable burn-rate alerts (alert-only), run chaos/replay tests.
Phase 3 (week 5): enable automated mitigations for burst-level actions behind a feature flag for a subset of tenants.
Phase 4 (week 6): remove feature flag after 1 week of stable behavior.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Quality metric design requires inputs from Applied ML; initial implementation will use heuristic signal (model log-likelihood and heuristic hallucination detector) with plan to replace with eval-derived signals.
- Borrow/repay semantics for regional reservations need billing alignment (product) to avoid overcharging.
- Determining concrete thresholds for different route classes will require historic-backing simulations; we propose default conservative values and per-customer tuning later.

Artifacts:
- Confluence doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/SLO+Quality+Curve+Spec (internal)
- Monitoring PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/3124 (WIP)
- Console RFC: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1slo-console-rfc (view-only link)
